features.name: Language Mapping setting (where the workspace language applies)
features.description: New `languageMapping` field on the workspace document and; `GET`/`PUT /workspaces/:workspaceId/language-mapping`. It stores which layers show in the; workspace language (`applyTo.platform` / `workspace` / `data`) and, per feature, which fields and; actions do (`features[featureId].items[componentId] = { kind, label, enabled }`). The language; itself is still `WORKSPACE_LANGUAGE`; the GET returns it with the provider for display. A PUT; replaces only the features it sends (`null` removes one). Nothing saved means everything; translates, which is the behaviour before this setting existed.

features.name: Platform entries
features.description: The language mapping also stores `platform` (CADP's own menus/screens, keyed by menu; node, plus `common-actions`), in the same entry shape as `features`, and returns it on GET. PUT; accepts `platform` the same way as `features` (`null` removes an entry).

features.name: Platform screen catalog
features.description: The mapping also stores `platformScreens`: the fields found on CADP's own screens, as; admins open them. Same entry shape, plus `path` on the entry and `type` on each item (Heading,; Tab, Field, Column, Placeholder, Button). GET returns it, and PUT accepts it like; `features`/`platform`. A `platform` entry may now carry `path`, which limits its switches to; that screen.

features.name: Routes for Workspace Settings › Language Mapping
features.description: New menu node "Language Mapping" (`submenu_015_language_mapping`) under Workspace; Settings, with View/Edit on `/rbac/master/workspaces/:workspaceId/language-mapping`. The GET is; also in the Dashboard's always-on View set, because every screen reads the mapping. Until menuData; is reseeded and roles are granted the new node, `authorise.middleware.js` aliases the GET/PUT to; the workspace environment-variables View/Edit right (whoever can change WORKSPACE_LANGUAGE can say; where it applies).

features.name: Author-set run order for a trigger's "run all connected paths" next steps
features.description: Workflow authors can now set the order in which a trigger's next steps run when Branching Mode is "Run all connected paths". Connections carry an optional `order` number; the parallel walker sorts the fan-out by it (numbered steps first, ascending; unnumbered steps after them in saved order). Invalid values (non-integer or negative) are reported by the workflow lint as `CONNECTION_INVALID_ORDER`.
features.impact: The steps run one after another, and a failing step stops the ones after it, so order matters (e.g. "GRN Reject": an upsert into the trigger's own feature ran first and changed the source record). Before this, order was the connection array order — which the save route sorts by connection id, i.e. effectively random.

features.name: Run Order list in the trigger's Branching Mode section
features.description: When a trigger's Branching Mode is "Run all connected paths", a "Run order" list of its next steps appears below the dropdown, with up/down arrows. Reordering numbers the trigger's outgoing connections 1..N (`connection.order`), saved with the workflow. Template workflows keep `order` when loaded.
features.impact: Lets authors control the sequence of the trigger's next steps; the backend runs them one after another in this order.

features.name: Workspace Settings › Language Mapping
features.description: New Workspace Settings section. It shows the workspace language (read-only; set under; Security › Environment Variables) and lets an admin choose where it applies: the Platform /; Workspace / Data layers, and per feature which fields and actions (toggle on = workspace language,; off = default language). The runtime translator (`documentTranslator.ts`) now takes an `allowed`; filter built by `languageMappingScope.ts`:; On a feature screen, inside `<main>`, a table cell or option is Data. A field or action label; switched off for that feature stays default. Everything else is Workspace.; Module and feature names are Workspace wherever they appear.; Everything else is Platform.; `tx()` labels follow the Platform switch. A saved mapping applies immediately via the; `workspace-language-mapping-saved` event.

features.name: Platform tab lists CADP's menus, screens and common buttons
features.description: The Platform side of Language Mapping was only a note. It now shows the platform menu; tree, built from the signed-in user's navigation permissions.; Selecting a menu lists it and its sub-menus/tabs under "Menus & Screens", each with its own; toggle.; "Actions" lists the buttons shared by every platform screen (Save, Cancel, Create, Delete…).; Saved under `platform` in the mapping (one entry per menu node, plus `common-actions`).; At runtime a platform label switched off stays in the default language, both on the page; (`languageMappingScope.ts`) and in `tx()`.

features.name: Platform screens list their fields
features.description: CADP's own screens have no field registry, so the app records their fields when a; screen is opened.; **Who records:** only a user who can edit Language Mapping (or, until RBAC is reseeded,; environment variables). On a platform screen, once the page has been quiet for 2s,; `platformScreenCapture.ts` reads it.; **What is read:** headings, tabs, labels, column headers, placeholders and buttons inside; `<main>`, in English even if the page is showing a translation. Table cells and; `data-no-translate` content are skipped.; **Where it goes:** into `platformScreens`. It is keyed by route pattern (ids → `:id`) plus the; section heading, and saved again only when new fields appear.; **Platform tab:** lists these under "Screens", grouped by first route segment, each with its; own Fields and Actions.; **Toggles:** saved under `platform` with the screen's `path`. They apply only on that screen; (`isPlatformLabelOff`). Menu and common-button switches still apply on every platform screen.

features.name: Platform menus list every field of their screen
features.description: Selecting a platform menu in Language Mapping now lists the fields its screen; shows, not only its tabs:; field labels, placeholders, column headers, headings, tab and option labels, and buttons; (under Actions); live items, one row each:; workspace environment variables and their groups and descriptions; workspace password policies; tenant variables and policies; platform variables and password policies

enhancements.description: The XLSX sample template now gives a table component's own dropdown columns (manual; options) a selectable in-cell dropdown on the table's sheet, the same way manual dropdowns on the; Records sheet already worked. Option values go on a per-table `<Table> Options` sheet.
enhancements.benefit: `getSampleTemplateStructure` only filled table-sheet `columnOptions` from; `buildReferenceTableColumnOptions` (a reference table's match columns), so every manual-dropdown; column inside a transaction/data table got `null` and no dropdown. New; `buildTableManualColumnOptions` / `_getManualTableColumnOptions` read the column's options from; root/basic/advanced/componentProps (mirroring the frontend's `resolveColumnOptions` /; `resolveColumnOptionSource`), only for a `manual` source — users/roles/org and feature sources are; skipped. Reference match-column options still take precedence for the same column.

enhancements.description: A filtered aggregate — `COUNT_RECORDS({field}, {status} == "closed")` and the rest of the `*_OF_RECORDS` family — now applies its filter against the **records** rather than a flat list of the field's values, and an aggregate chosen from **"Saved records"** on the current feature now resolves its source instead of reading nothing. `== 0` no longer matches every record, `!= 0` no longer matches none, and `> N` no longer matches nothing.
enhancements.benefit: Two defects combined, and both had to be fixed for a filtered count to be right.; 1. **The array path won.** The external resolver replaces an aggregate's field token with `__aggN`, a flat list of that field's values — fine for an unfiltered total, but a filter's tokens name *fields of a record*, and a list of values has no record to read them from. The filter tokens resolved to nothing and were substituted as `0`, so every comparison was really against zero.; 2. **No feature resolved.** `pickAggregateFeatureId` consulted only `selectModuleSets`, which lists the features a user explicitly added. A same-feature aggregate picked as "Saved records" emits no set at all — the token map is what records it, as `source: 'external'` plus the owning feature — so no feature resolved and the aggregate's records were never fetched.; Observed on DEV before the fix, over 4 records all with non-zero values: `== 0` → 4, `!= 0` → 0, `> 0` → 0.

enhancements.description: A formula aggregate (`COUNT_RECORDS`, `SUM_OF_RECORDS`, and the other `*_OF_RECORDS` functions) now also honours the role's **View** scope — `Own` or `Group` — not just its Data Access Control filter. Two paths are covered: the cross-feature record scan and the same-feature aggregate push-down pipeline. The aggregate and the user's own record list now report the same set.
enhancements.benefit: Two different mechanisms narrow a feature's rows, and they live in different places. The DAC **rule** already reaches every read, including aggregate pipelines, through the global plugin (`config/db/session-param-plugin.js`). The `view` **scope** is not a rule — it never appears in `permissionIndex.filter` — so it is applied by the route as `_metadata.createdById`. A formula has no route to inherit it from, so a `View: Own` user's aggregate counted every creator's records. Measured on a test feature: a role set to `View: Own` was shown the full workspace total while its own list returned only its own rows.

enhancements.description: `TIME_DIFF({field}, "10:00", "hours")` now fails validation when `{field}` is a **Text** field, with `TYPE_MISMATCH` on argument 1. A time written as a quoted literal — `TIME_DIFF({end}, "10:00", "hours")` — and a real TIME field both continue to validate as before.
enhancements.benefit: The validator's time check exempted any `string` argument, because a quoted literal such as `"10:00"` is how a time argument is normally written. But a Text field also resolves to `string`, so `TIME_DIFF({city}, ...)` passed validation and then produced `NaN` at runtime — the error surfaced as a wrong number in the form rather than as a validation message. The two cases are distinguishable in the AST: a quoted time is a `ConstantNode`, a field reference is not. The exemption is therefore narrowed to literals rather than removed.

enhancements.description: The badge icon on the AI assistant's welcome card now shows a tooltip on hover and announces itself to a screen reader. The text names what the panel is for: **Create with AI**, **Ask about the platform**, or the read-only variant's own title.
enhancements.benefit: The icon was rendered `aria-hidden` inside a bare `div`, so it had neither a hover tooltip nor an accessible name — QA filed it as "FAQ icon does not display tooltip on mouse hover" (#1740). Naming it is also the honest thing for a screen reader: the icon states the panel's purpose, and a decorative hidden icon states nothing.

enhancements.description: Switching the AI assistant between the **Create** and **Ask** tabs now returns you to the conversation you were last in on that tab, instead of blanking the transcript back to the welcome card.
enhancements.benefit: The tab switch set the active thread to `null` outright, so the transcript fell back to the empty welcome state until a manual refresh — even though the thread still existed (the server held it for Create, `localStorage` for Ask) and **Show chat history** still listed it (#1726). The thread was never lost; the widget just stopped pointing at it.

enhancements.description: An aggregate built through the guided **Formula Wizard** now reads the stored records of the feature it names — including when that feature is the one the formula lives on — and a value typed into the wizard's condition no longer silently matches nothing.
enhancements.benefit: Two defects, both on the wizard path only (the field picker was already correct).; 1. **Wrong token source (#1441 / #1623-#1638).** The wizard stamped `source: 'local'` on every token belonging to the current feature. For an aggregate that is wrong: "This form" holds exactly one value, and aggregating one value is meaningless, so the engine had no record set and returned its empty fallback — a same-feature aggregate read `0.00` however many records existed. The field picker has always carried this distinction (`readsSavedRecords` → `source: 'external'`); the wizard did not, so the guided path could not produce a working same-feature aggregate at all.; 2. **Double-quoted values (#1762).** A value typed into the wizard was wrapped in quotes unconditionally, so typing `"Biscuits"` — quotes included — produced `""Biscuits""`, a literal that matches nothing. The condition was valid and simply never matched.

enhancements.description: A formula whose entire expression is `YEAR(...)` now displays as a whole year — `2026`, not `2026.00` — in the form field, the table cell and the list/view. The rule is anchored to the whole expression: `YEAR({d}) + 1` and `ROUND(YEAR({d}) / 2)` are ordinary numbers again and keep their configured formatting.
enhancements.benefit: The numeric display default is two decimal places, which is right for money and wrong for a calendar year (#1668). Three formatters disagreed about it — the shared engine formatter, the form field and the transaction table each had their own path — so the same formula could read `2026` in one place and `2026.00` in another.

enhancements.description: Removes the rule that made a bare `YEAR(...)` formula render without decimals regardless of the field's configuration. A year now follows the field's Number Format like every other numeric formula. The one part of the earlier change that is **kept** is the `decimalPlaces` clamp correction: a configured 0 now means zero decimals instead of silently becoming one.
enhancements.benefit: The earlier change special-cased `YEAR(...)` so it always rendered as `2026`. That overrode an explicit design choice — the platform already lets a designer turn decimals off (Advanced → Number Format → uncheck Decimals), and the two-decimal default is applied to every numeric formula on purpose, which is why `3 + 2` reads `5.00`. Special-casing one function made a year behave differently from every other number without anyone asking for it, and it made the display depend on the expression's shape rather than on the field's settings. **#1668 is a configuration answer, not a defect.**

enhancements.description: When the image picker refuses a file before uploading it — too large, or the wrong format — it now shows a short message naming the file and the reason, e.g. `photo.png — File is larger than 10MB`. Previously the picker simply did nothing.
enhancements.benefit: The size/format check happens before the file becomes an upload, so a rejected file never enters the preview list and had no thumbnail to hang an error badge on; the only trace was a `console.error` the user never sees (#1708). QA filed it as "6.68 MB PNG: not uploaded, no error/validation message" — the check was working, but silently.

configChanges: OCR.Space key is read from the vault on deployed pods

`OCR_SPACE_API_KEY` is removed from `.env.production`, so deployed pods load it from the vault secret; `ocr-space-api-key` (mounted as `dev-ocr-space-api-key` or `ocr-space-api-key`) through the mapping that already; exists in `src/config/runtime-bootstrap.js`. `.env.development` / `.env.uat` keep the key for local runs (CSI off).

A value in the env file wins over the vault, so the vault mapping was never used and the live key sat in; git. **Deploy:** the `cadp-dev-kv` SecretProviderClass must expose `ocr-space-api-key` (or `cadp-dev-env` must set; `OCR_SPACE_API_KEY`) before this ships — otherwise OCR returns "OCR service is not configured (missing; OCR_SPACE_API_KEY)". The key has been in git history, so rotate it when it moves to the vault.
Workflow OCR node reads the server OCR.Space key from the vault

The OCR node's server-side OCR.Space key (`OCR_SPACE_API_KEY`) is now loaded from the vault at startup,; the same way client-ws loads it, so OCR nodes without their own API key use OCR.Space instead of falling back; to the lower-quality local Tesseract OCR. The service reads the mounted secret `dev-ocr-space-api-key`, then; `ocr-space-api-key`; a value already in the environment still wins. The key is optional — startup does not fail; without it.

The node falls back to `process.env.OCR_SPACE_API_KEY`, but this service had no vault mapping and no env; entry for it, so the server key was never set and every key-less OCR node silently used Tesseract; (`usedFallback: true`). Deploy: the `cadp-dev-kv` SecretProviderClass must expose `ocr-space-api-key` (the same; secret client-ws already maps) to the workflow pod.
